reader_summaries.summary: Hot path architecture: heartbeat_core.py (live, GAMMA_CORE_ARMED=1 + GAMMA_CORE_MANAGES_EXITS=1 confirmed set by the actual Task-Scheduler-launched wrapper) ticks ~every 1-2min RTH, runs engine_cli's score+15-gate stack, and on ENTER places a simple marketable-limit option order (never a broker bracket -- Alpaca rejects those for options, code 42210000). ALL exit protection -- catastrophe cap, TP1, runner, chart-stop, time-stop -- is therefore a pure python decision made only while heartbeat_core.py is alive and ticking; there is no resting broker-side stop order at any point. The compensating safety nets are: heal-engine.ps1 (re-fires a dead process during RTH, with a hard-won guard against the 2026-08-14 double-entry race) and EOD-flatten (15:52-15:55 ET, both a deterministic script and an LLM-based one). Sizing/kill-switch doctrine (CLAUDE.md Rules 5/6) is nominally 30%/50%-of-equity, but the code actually enforces the TIGHTER of that and two flat-dollar floors added 2026-08-29 ($1,000/trade notional, $400/day loss) that CLAUDE.md's rule text never mentions -- at current ~$5.6-5.8K equity these dollar floors are what actually bind for BOTH accounts, converging Safe and Bold's effective risk envelopes despite their differently-worded doctrine. Start-of-day equity capture is genuinely well-engineered (deterministic, broker-verified, explicitly un-blockable by an LLM outage). The single most important discovery this pass: the manual 'kill-switch' safety net that EOD-flatten is supposed to set when it can't verify Bold is flat (Alpaca aggressive MCP unreachable, which happened for real on both 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-01) writes to the wrong filename (kill-switch.json vs. the kill-switch heartbeat_core.py actually checks) and is consumed by zero code in the repo -- so on both real occurrences this week, the account believed it had halted pending manual review and had not. This is the concrete, field-verified shape of the go_live_gate's flagged 'dead_mans_switch_open_position_on_process_death = NO TEST FOUND' operational gap (already tracked HIGH/pending in queue.md), and it just fired twice while trading real paper capital, only staying harmless by luck. Verdict: the hot-path engine's entry/gate logic (idempotency claim files, fill reconciliation with bounded retries, stale-bar detection, per-account SOD capture) is careful and mostly well-defended, but the exit-protection story has a real, now-demonstrated single point of failure that should be closed before any live-money arming, and EOD-flatten -- the single most safety-critical script in the system -- should not be LLM-mediated with no deterministic fallback.

reader_summaries.summary: The fleet's declared architecture (a shared strategies.py REGISTRY of 3 validated edges, run on every arm via 2x3 grid of gate x sizing profiles) does not match what is actually live. Only 1 of the 3 REGISTRY strategies (ribbon_ride) currently fires on any of the 4 active arms (safe-2, bold-2, safe-3, risky-1) -- vwap_continuation and vwap_reclaim_failed_break are both administratively disarmed via params.json's extra_setup_exec_armed, which since a 2026-08-12 fix gates the fleet path too. This is the concrete mechanism behind the fresh-fact r=0.846 fleet correlation: it isn't just a shared signal, it's literally one entry strategy in four risk wrappers. A second, independent finding: bold-2's strike-tier ATM wire was legitimately reverted 2026-08-20 (a pre-registered falsification rail triggered negative, n=25, -$808 vs +$406 for the OTM control) back to OTM-2/OTM-3 -- but this reversion is only visible in the code; aggressive/params.json's own doc field and crypto/lib/strike_selection.py's docstring both still claim the ATM wire is live, and this landed inside bold-2's go-live measurement window. Fresh decision-log grep confirms the practical cost is real: bold-2 hit SKIP_MIN_PREMIUM_FLOOR 27 times in the last 10 sessions vs 0 for the three still-ATM arms. On the params-consumer side, dead_knob_audit.py (run fresh, redirected to scratchpad to stay read-only) confirms premium_stop_pct/tp1_premium_pct/tp1_qty_fraction are SHADOWED in both params files by strategies.py's hardcoded ExitShape -- so CLAUDE.md's 'tp1_qty_fraction 0.8 Safe / 0.667 Bold' line describes a dead value; the real live ribbon_ride TP1 shape (100%/sell 66.7%, with a 2026-08-10 pre-TP1 ladder at +50%/+75%) is identical for both accounts. On the positive side: the ATM strike + $0.30 premium floor combination is empirically confirmed working right now (0 floor-blocks on the 3 ATM arms vs high floor-block rates whenever an arm trades OTM), and the config freeze is holding cleanly with 2+ days of margin verified directly via git status. The params-consumer reconciliation test suite passes 7/7. Net verdict: the fleet's statistical evidence going into the real-money decision is more concentrated (fewer genuinely independent strategies, less strike diversity than documented) and has more undocumented mid-window regime changes (bold-2's strike tier) than the accounts.json/CLAUDE.md paper trail currently discloses.

reader_summaries.summary: This subsystem is Gamma's raw execution ledger (automation/state/fills-ledger.jsonl: 1,200 fills, 2026-06-26 to 09-01, 62 dates, 6 arms) and the FIFO round-trip reconstruction feeding the go-live gate and SIGNATURE.md. I re-derived it independently using automation/state/fleet/fills_fifo.py's mine_real_arm_fills() (imported verbatim, primary method) plus a parameterized copy for manual fills. Engine-attributed round trips: n=385 book-wide, WR 25.7%, PF 1.058, net +$1,220; era split at the 2026-08-11 ladder-ratchet ship is sharp -- pre n=229/28 days net -$1,663 (PF 0.868), post n=156/15 days net +$2,883 (PF 1.338, WR 37.8%), exactly matching SIGNATURE.md's own quoted figure. I cross-validated against analysis/trades-enriched.jsonl (385/385 engine rows matched, 0 pnl or daily-total mismatches) and reproduced go_live_gate.py's exact bootstrap methodology for safe-2, landing on ci_lower_2.5=0.333 through two independent paths -- confirming the gate's RED verdict is real math, not a bug. The positive edge concentrates almost entirely in one setup (BULLISH_RECLAIM_RIDE_THE_RIBBON, +$3,435) and calls over puts (+$2,380 vs -$1,160), and all 4 active arms share the identical single best day (2026-08-04, 20-26% of each arm's gross profit-day dollars). The entire sample, winning and losing eras alike, was earned in low-VIX (14.7-20.6, only 3/52 days>20) mildly-uptrending SPY conditions with no genuine crash tested. Forward arithmetic: pushing safe-2's CI-lower above 1.0 by ~09-29 needs an added ~$166/day (zero-variance best case) against an existing -$7.20/day mean -- a swing none of the 4 arms has ever sustained, making the '08-29 plan / GREEN by early October' framing arithmetically unsupported under the current config freeze. Verdict: the gate is trustworthy, the edge (where it exists) is real and reproducible from raw fills but thin, single-setup-concentrated, single-day-concentrated, and entirely untested outside a calm regime.

reader_summaries.summary: Project Gamma's validation machinery is a prereg-first research discipline (121 analysis/recommendations/*prereg*.json files) meant to commit to a method before looking, run it, and record a named-nail verdict per fable-judgment/02-VALIDATION.md's kill ladder -- but the "run it and record a verdict" half is demonstrably not keeping pace with the "commit to it" half: a census found 15 preregs frozen 18-27 days ago and explicitly self-labeled "NOT RUN," with zero reference anywhere in setup/backtest/automation, corroborated by 13 of 14 recommendations-log.jsonl entries from the last 30 days still sitting "pending." Two concrete data-integrity/trust defects sit inside the machinery itself: (1) the queue's own HIGH-priority PLANNED-STOP-IS-NOT-THE-EXECUTED-STOP item (79% mismatch between logged planned_stop and the stop that actually fired) is still unfixed, silently corrupting any stop-keyed study; (2) the repo's one dedicated broker-truth fidelity anchor test (harness_fidelity_anchor.py, the "V9" gate) is explicitly, by design, unable to validate structure/ribbon exits -- CLAUDE.md's own primary exit mode since 2026-06-18 -- so its reassuring 94.5%-sign-agreement number says little about the exit logic that actually governs most live decisions. The MAP.md-reported "58 broken wikilinks" turned out, on inspection of obsidian_vault_sync.py, to be a pure generator bug (the link-health scanner only ever indexes .md files and blindly appends ".md" to extensionless targets) rather than missing content -- all 4 sampled "broken" preregs exist exactly where their links point. On the positive side, recency_check.py's 2026-08-08 fix (commit 56c2cdc9) that moved the Discord-facing LicenseMonitor gate onto the sound walk_exit_manager engine is a genuinely well-executed, narrowly-scoped, guard-tested remediation -- but the queue item describing that same defect is itself stale, still open, and no longer matches reality for the part that reaches J. Structurally, nothing in the codebase enforces consulting a "graveyard" of killed ideas before Chef cooks a new candidate or a new prereg is filed -- doctrine names the goal ("prevent zombie resurrections") but the mechanism is only soft LLM memory. Overall verdict: the validation machinery's individual instruments are often well-built when someone builds them, but there is no closed-loop system tracking whether a filed hypothesis actually gets resolved, whether a fixed defect gets its queue entry closed, or whether a fidelity claim's scope is honestly bounded -- all three gaps compound to make it hard for anyone (Claude or J) to trust an aggregate "the validation stack says GO" statement without re-deriving it from scratch, which is exactly the state this audit found.

reader_summaries.summary: Ops/autonomy layer is mechanically sound in its individual pieces (quiet-mode's evening blackout is well-designed and verified firing correctly live; the deterministic eod_flatten.py Core script works and proved itself today) but the SEAMS between pieces are where real risk lives. The single most material finding: right now, as this audit runs, the Bold/aggressive account carries a LIVE, UNRESOLVED "manual intervention required" kill-switch (2nd consecutive day) because the LLM-based EOD flattener couldn't reach mcp__alpaca_aggressive__ at 15:55 ET -- and this state is completely invisible to engine-health.json's fused GREEN verdict, which reads different, stale files instead. A separate Core check 3 minutes earlier did confirm the account flat, but nothing wires that confirmation back to the kill-switch, so the alarm sits unresolved and mis-surfaced as a low-key ".ps1 timeout" hygiene note rather than a position-safety flag. Zoomed out, the conductor's own STAGE-1 priority order structurally explains why this class of issue (and the two go-live-gate-blocking HIGH items, DEAD-MANS-SWITCH and PROD-SHADOW) keep not getting picked: an unbounded, continuously-refilled self-audit-gap backlog sits ahead of queue.md HIGH items in the priority list, and confirmed via ~9 visible fires (08-30->09-01), none touched either blocking item. A second, independent scheduling defect (quiet-mode's evening blackout silently disabling the documented 20:30 ET conductor fire) cuts nightly autonomous throughput by roughly a third, undocumented, likely contributing to autonomy-metric.json's 'trend: regressing'. None of this changes the underlying strategy edge, but it directly explains why the operational side of the go-live gate keeps failing despite ~9 fires/3 days of nominal autonomous work, and it demonstrates -- live, today, in paper trading -- exactly the failure class the go-live gate's one remaining operational blocker exists to catch.

reader_summaries.summary: Project Gamma's path from a GREEN go-live gate to real dollars has gaps the gate itself doesn't measure. The most severe: Alpaca structurally rejects broker-side stop/bracket orders for options, so every protective exit (TP, catastrophe cap, time-stop) is enforced entirely by software ticking every heartbeat cycle -- which makes the already-known missing dead-man's-switch not a slow-recovery problem but a zero-backstop problem. Separately, and apparently un-tracked anywhere in the queue, the live engine still hardcodes feed=iex and runs a filter (buyer-pressure, vol_mult=0.7) that a 2026-08-07 research doc proved was calibrated on SIP volume but evaluated on IEX (~3.6% of real tape volume), flipping roughly a third of otherwise-refused elite setups -- unfixed today, frozen until ~09-29, and not fixable by simply buying real-time data without an accompanying code change. The one instrument that applies real regulatory fees to real fills (cost_model.py) shows the book net-LOSING money once fees and even a conservative exit-slippage assumption are applied (-$2,200.82 to -$5,068.82 over 289 round trips) and hasn't been re-run in two weeks, so nobody knows if the newer 'post-ladder' era survives it. Exit-side execution quality has never once been measured against a real quote (the recorder built for it has zero rows in its life). SPY-options tax treatment (ordinary short-term gains, wash-sale exposure, no CPA consulted) is a genuine, currently-zero-coverage blind spot. On the positive side: the PDT/regulatory research is exceptional (primary-sourced, dated, live-field-verified -- FINRA's $25k rule is confirmed gone for these accounts), and a fresh github_audit.py run this session is clean (GREEN, 0 findings, secrets properly gitignored). The LIVE-FLIP-RUNBOOK is unusually thorough but has real, unaddressed gaps: no automated kill-switch-trip revert (the 'no discretion' abort promise is manual), no phone/SMS alert path to J (Discord only, previously muted), no duplicate-order-idempotency statement, no key-rotation cadence, no funding/withdrawal policy, and an unverified EOD-flatten pin-risk buffer. A fully-built, tested, dollar-material policy (DAILY-PREMIUM-BUDGET-J-CALL, +$3,844 on the historical tape) sits awaiting a J judgment call, frozen until the config freeze lifts. Overall: the statistical gate is RED for good reason, but even a future statistical GREEN would still be sitting on top of several structural and measurement gaps this domain surfaced that the gate itself does not check.

reader_summaries.summary: Doctrine and code have diverged in several places that were flagged in prior audits and never closed, plus one new integrity gap in go_live_gate.py itself. The rule-break/mistakes logging pipeline (automation/state/rule-breaks.jsonl, journal/mistakes.md) has been effectively dead since 2026-06-15/06-20 despite 1,200+ fills since, so go_live_gate.py's "Behavioural PASS: 0 rule breaks" is measuring an empty pipe, not clean behavior -- and unlike the sibling instrument live_readiness.py (which reports this exact gap as UNKNOWN), go_live_gate.py converts it to an unconditional PASS. CLAUDE.md's Rule 7 (PDT) text and "Goal: $5K->$10K->$25K+" line are still the exact stale text ROADMAP.md's 2026-08-18 audit flagged for a Rule-9 rewrite -- 14 days later they're unfixed, even though the sibling doc risk-rules.md and the Live-threshold line three lines below in the SAME file were both corrected in that window, meaning this is a dropped escalation, not an untouched file. decisions.jsonl is dead since 2026-06-25 (63 lines, last row literally says "LLM did not persist a decisions row this tick") while core-decisions.jsonl is the real live ledger (36,599 lines, appending today). CLAUDE.md still cites decisions.jsonl 3x as if it were current. On FOCUS-DOCTRINE's "level interaction, bounded search" claim: the workhorse (ribbon_ride, REJECT/RECLAIM at a chart level) genuinely satisfies it, but 5 of the 7 extra_signals wired into every live tick (bollinger_squeeze, gap_and_go, vix_regime_dayside, double_bottom_base_quiet, level_break_first_strike) have produced ZERO real trades ever across 391 closed round trips -- 80% concentration in the two ribbon setups, which is the mechanical reason the 5-arm fleet correlates at r=0.846 (already known) and is already tracked as a HIGH open item (WATCHER-LANE-PROVENANCE-AUDIT, filed 08-23, still pending). Doc-hygiene: DOC-ARCHITECTURE's own fold protocol (written after a "159-file sprawl" in June) is not being followed -- analysis/deep-research/ is now 154 files, 139 (90%) created in August alone, zero folded or deleted. On the positive side: the doctrine-hooks enforcement layer (setup/hooks/gamma_doctrine.py) is verifiably fail-open with a pre-registered freeze-override token and 187/187 tests passing fresh this session (the doc understates this at 49, itself stale but in the safe direction), and the C31 "never average down" lesson is a real, tested code guard (is_flat_spy_options, 9/9 passing, no-bypass signature pinned) -- not just prose. The one clear BLIND_SPOT: go_live_gate.py's own behavioural criterion explicitly SKIPS (not fabricates) any check for sizing-up-after-loss -- the single costliest documented historical pattern (C31: -$17,461 on 3+ lots) -- so nothing in the go-live decision path currently measures whether recent trading recurred that exact behavior at the account level.

reader_summaries.summary: Project Gamma's codebase is a 720K-line, one-person-plus-agents Python rig with real engineering strengths (a genuinely single broker surface in fleet_broker.py; a mature, incident-hardened Windows headless-subprocess launcher) sitting alongside accumulating structural debt that is now demonstrably causing undetected defects, not just hygiene complaints. The clearest concrete finding: the AGGRESSIVE account's EOD-flatten safety net failed to broker-verify a flat position on 2 consecutive trading days (08-31, 09-01) because its MCP connection didn't come up inside the ~2-5 minute window it had -- this is the dead-man's-switch gap the orchestrator's fresh go_live_gate run already flags as untested, caught here as a live recurring incident rather than a theoretical gap. Separately, live decision-gating state (current-position*.json, kill-switch markers) remains git-tracked despite doctrine (L214/L233) explicitly warning this causes silent state reverts, in a repo currently carrying 3,014 modified tracked files and 38 stale/orphaned branches. On code quality: 7 hot-path files breach the project's own 800-line cap by up to 4.1x, and the single highest-complexity function in the repo is the live order-placement function itself (521 lines, cyclomatic complexity 82) -- and this audit found a concrete bug living in exactly that kind of complexity: 3 tests have been silently RED since 2026-08-29 (pre-freeze) because a newer risk cap (tight-ladder max_contracts_per_entry) defeats an older cap-interaction guard (cheap-contract-qty-boost), undetected because the 'fast' test suite has grown to 11,096 tests and does not complete within any reasonable session (est. 25-30 min, no parallelization installed). The designated cold-start architecture doc has been stale since 2026-06-25 and omits the entire fleet layer (3 of 4 currently-scored arms). Overall verdict: the engineering discipline exists (guard tests, incident-documented fixes, single-broker-surface architecture) but has been outrun by the system's growth rate, and the test suite meant to catch regressions is now too large to actually run, which is itself why a real regression sat unnoticed through the config freeze.

This audit could not find a broker-side confirmation in the files read.

reader_summaries.summary: The ledger stack itself is more trustworthy than the surface-level numbers suggest, but it rests on two genuinely dirty layers. journal/trades.csv (the human-facing "if it's not in the journal it didn't happen" log) is actively corrupting via unescaped JSON in archetype_match_json -- a defect logged once (2026-07-18, 2 rows) and left unfixed; this audit found 25 rows through 2026-08-25, meaning the bug is ongoing and worse than tracked. Separately, exit-fill slippage is essentially unmeasured: quote_recorder.py is 4 days old with ~1 day of real coverage (388/391 trades have no quote match), and go_live_gate.py's cost-adjusted criterion doesn't even consume that data -- it uses a fixed, never-validated 2c/contract assumption. On the "manual trading contaminates the engine's evidence" question the answer is reassuring: of safe-2's 165 "manual" fills, 155 are a documented $10 nightly crypto broker-canary (dress_rehearsal.py) and only 10 are real option fills, all from the project's first 3 weeks -- current edge measurement is not contaminated by hand trading. That canary, however, runs inside the LIVE safe-2 account slated to go live with real money first, directly contradicting the crypto twin's own "never touch a fleet/core account" rule, and leaves floating-point dust that makes the "broker=truth" pnl-statement.json report 16 phantom open positions that a live broker check this session confirmed do not exist. core-decisions.jsonl tick integrity is excellent (772/772 exact for 10 straight days, 89/90 PLACED orders match a fill) and the attribution design is sound -- both worth protecting. Key-levels.json partially implements J's "levels are zones" doctrine six weeks late (a third of levels still on the unvalidated default width, the multi-day-memory family still point levels) and carries two 64-day-stale expired levels that a downstream engine-side guard, thankfully, neutralizes. Net verdict: the money-path plumbing (tick cadence, order-to-fill linkage, engine/manual attribution) is solid; the measurement/reporting layer around it (trade journal, slippage evidence, level-zone validation) has real, fixable holes that should close before leaning hard on any of today's headline numbers.
open_questions: Was journal/trades.csv's writer (the log-trade skill / whatever script actually appends rows) ever changed to route archetype_match_json through csv.writer, or is the underlying bug from 2026-07-18 genuinely still live in the writer code today? I traced the SYMPTOM (25 corrupted rows through 08-25) exhaustively but did not locate/read the specific writer script itself (no log_trade.py found by filename; likely implemented as a skill/inline snippet rather than a standalone .py file) to confirm the exact still-broken code path.

Does any currently-scheduled production script actually crash or silently mis-attribute data because of the trades.csv corruption right now (i.e. is this WYSIWYG-broken today, or just a latent landmine)? I found one pandas.read_csv call on a generic trades_csv parameter in backtest/tools/entry_experiment.py but did not confirm what path it's called with in practice.

Is the dress_rehearsal.py $10 crypto canary intentionally accepted by J as an exception to the twin's dedicated-account rule, or was this simply never surfaced to him? This changes whether it's a WRONG or an accepted RIGHT-with-caveats.

Has anyone computed what fraction of the 25 corrupted trades.csv rows are 'engine' vs 'manual'/aggressive-account trades, and whether any of them are among the trades cited in analysis/winner-autopsies/SIGNATURE.md's specific-trade narratives (which would mean a headline stat is quoting a row with unreliable late-column fields)?

Given quote-tape coverage is essentially brand new, what is the plan/timeline for accumulating enough real quote data (weeks?) to actually validate or replace the fixed 2c/contract slippage assumption before any live-money decision leans on the cost-adjusted PF number?

reader_summaries.summary: Devil's-advocate read of the whole go-live path, built on the orchestrator's fresh gate run plus my own re-computation from analysis/trades-enriched.jsonl (266 engine round trips, 4 active arms, 40 trading days) and SPY 5m bars through 2026-09-01. The subsystem under review is the PLAN itself: freeze config 08-31, score 20 clean September days with go_live_gate.py, arm one live account in early October. Verdict: the plan's arithmetic does not close. Scored the way the gate is coded (full history pooled), appending 20 more days drawn from the post-ladder era yields P(pass) of 0.00 (safe-2), 0.02 (bold-2), 0.13 (safe-3), 0.10 (risky-1), 0.03 (book); even a standalone 20-day window from the good era passes the as-traded+ex-best-day bar only 9-39% of the time, and the TIGHT-LADDER prereg independently registers a 40-day window closing 2026-10-30 with a 'November live question' -- two frozen clocks that disagree. The measured positive era is thin and beta-shaped: book P&L correlates +0.23 with SPY open-to-close return, +$2,473 on SPY-up days vs -$481 on down days, calls made $3,125 on up days vs $123 on down days, and the post-08-11 era minus its two best days (08-27/08-28) is -$154 over the other 13 sessions; no whole-engine null (random-entry-same-exit or buy-ATM-daily) has ever been run. The sizing story is better than doctrine text suggests: the 08-29 tight-ladder controls (5 contracts / $1,000 / -$400 day stop) are live in params.json and risk_gate.py and cap a $5.5K account's worst trade near 9% and worst day near 7% -- protect them -- but CLAUDE.md Rule 5/6, the runbook's -30% abort, and the runbook's 1-contract Day-1 ramp (blocked by MIN_CONTRACTS>=3 in risk_gate) are all stale against that reality. The go-live candidate named by LIVE-FLIP-RUNBOOK (safe-2) is the arm the 08-29 handoff schedules for retirement at window close, and it has negative trade-level Kelly. The two HIGH gate blockers from the 08-29 review (dead-man's-switch, prod-shadow) received zero fires because the conductor's picker reads the config freeze as 'no ready non-frozen SPY item'. The '281 manual fills' headline is a labeling artifact (broker_fills.py tags every crypto fill 'manual'; only 15 SPY-option manual fills exist, last 2026-07-17), but there is still no J-side circuit -- the engine is designed to adopt manual positions, not refuse them. Honest n for the frozen engine is 2 sessions; honest n for the post-ladder engine is 15 days, 2 of which carry all the profit. If 'real money before 2027' is the goal, the decision to put in front of J now is a bounded fixed-dollar live pilot defined as the prod-shadow itself (the only instrument that can measure paper-vs-live fills), or an honest 'not this year' -- not a green gate that the math says will not arrive.
open_questions: Which clock governs the live decision: go_live_gate 20-day window (~09-29) or PREREG-TIGHT-LADDER 40-day window (10-30)? Nobody has reconciled them.
Does the engine beat a random-entry-same-exit null and a buy-ATM-call-daily baseline on the post-08-11 days? Never computed.
What is the live Alpaca options data tier and does the live account get OPRA or indicative quotes? Runbook 2.4 still open.
Where is the 'TASK A2' compounding bootstrap (12.4%/3.6% ruin) that LIVE-FLIP-RUNBOOK cites? Not found in repo.
What mechanism makes the conductor treat DEAD-MANS-SWITCH / PROD-SHADOW as frozen items? Behaviour observed in STATUS, code path not traced.
Which producer places the daily ~$10 BTC/USD pair on the safe-2 (and other arm) accounts, and should those rows be attributed 'canary' rather than 'manual'?
If J wants real money in 2026 regardless of gate color, what fixed-dollar pilot size and abort list would he accept -- this is OP-0 #1 territory and needs his answer, not Gamma's.

survivors.title: No broker-side stop on options + the manual 'kill-switch' safety net is a no-op (wrong filename, never read) -- confirmed by 2 consecutive real near-misses
survivors.detail: Options positions get NO broker-side stop/TP order at all (Alpaca rejects brackets for options); every protective exit is a python decision made by heartbeat_core.py's live tick loop. If that process dies with a position open, heal-engine.ps1 only restarts the process (RTH-only, 8-min staleness threshold, 4-min cooldown -- up to ~8-12 min unprotected) and never flattens directly. The declared backstop for the unhealable case is the EOD-flatten prompt's instruction to write a manual kill-switch and halt trading pending human review. That backstop is itself broken: the prompt is told to create `automation/state/kill-switch`, but on both 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-01 (today) it actually wrote `automation/state/kill-switch.json` -- a different filename. heartbeat_core.py's real check is `(STATE / "kill-switch").exists()` (no extension). Grepping the entire repo for any .py/.ps1 consumer of `kill-switch.json` returns zero files. So on both days the account believed it had halted itself pending manual verification of Bold's flat state, and it had not -- the engine would have kept trading bold-2 unimpeded. It was harmless both times purely because bold-2 happened to be flat (independently confirmed via the safe-lane's own EOD_FLATTEN_NOOP check at 15:52:01 today). Separately, even a correctly-named file would trip BOTH accounts at once (`STATE/'kill-switch'` is a single global path, unlike the correctly per-account circuit-breaker.json), violating Rule 5's 'Safe halting does NOT halt Bold' isolation promise.

survivors.title: Every open option position has ZERO broker-side backstop -- all stops are software-only, and the dead-man's-switch that would compensate is confirmed still missing
survivors.detail: Alpaca rejects complex/bracket/OTO/OCO orders for options (HTTP 422, code 42210000) -- confirmed in memory-mirror/project_alpaca_options_no_brackets.md and corroborated by atomic_bracket_guard.py's own docstring, which exists only as a post-hoc naked-position DETECTOR, not a broker-side stop. Every TP1/catastrophe-cap/time-stop is enforced by exit_manager reading a fresh quote and firing a market_sell EVERY HEARTBEAT TICK. This means the already-known dead-man's-switch gap (go_live_gate.py operational FAIL, Fable 08-29 review's #1 finding, still open per this session's fresh gate run) is worse than 'recovery is slow' -- if heartbeat_core dies with a position open, there is LITERALLY NOTHING on the broker side protecting it (no GTC stop order, no OCO leg) until either the same software stack's EOD-flatten script fires hours later, or a human notices. This raises the bar for what the DMS build needs to be: an independent watchdog process is not optional hardening, it is the ONLY thing standing between a dead engine and an unbounded loss on a real position.

survivors.title: SPY options tax treatment (ordinary short-term gains + wash-sale exposure) is not modeled or considered anywhere -- and the structural alternative (SPX/XSP, Section 1256) exists at Alpaca only in paper
survivors.detail: SPX and XSP options qualify as Section 1256 'nonequity options' -- 60/40 blended long/short capital-gains treatment regardless of holding period, mark-to-market at year-end, and explicitly EXEMPT from the wash-sale rule. SPY, being an option on an ETF share rather than the index directly, gets neither: ordinary short-term gains taxed at up to ~37-40.8% (vs an illustrative ~26.8% blended rate under 1256), AND full wash-sale exposure. At Gamma's real trade cadence (~500+ round trips/yr across the fleet, many same-day same-symbol re-entries after a loss -- exactly the wash-sale trigger pattern), this is not a rounding error. A repo-wide grep for 'wash' or '1256' outside a single disclosed-but-explicitly-not-computed docstring paragraph in cost_model.py returns nothing -- there is no tax P&L estimate anywhere, and no evidence a CPA has been consulted. Note: Alpaca added PAPER-ONLY support for SPX/SPXW/XSP on 2026-07-23 with no committed live date, so switching to the tax-advantaged instrument is not currently actionable even if desired -- this is reported as an unconsidered structural fact, not a recommendation to change strategy.

gaps.angle: The broker's view of a LIVE Alpaca account: expiration-day liquidation/DNE policy, live options market-data entitlement, market-order acceptance on options, and how Alpaca PAPER simulates option fills vs live
gaps.summary: Nobody in this audit had checked Alpaca's own published expiration-day risk-management policy for options, and it materially changes the live-money picture. Alpaca's docs (fetched live this session) state that starting at 3:30pm ET on expiry day, Alpaca evaluates every position expiring that day and, for a long option that is ITM but whose account lacks buying power to exercise, WILL LIQUIDATE IT ITSELF, on its own timing and price -- and may sweep 'slightly OTM' positions too. Every core arm's equity ($5.6K-$6.5K) is nowhere near the $60K+ notional needed to exercise even one SPY contract, so any live ITM 0DTE long open at 3:30pm ET falls straight into Alpaca's forced-liquidation branch. The engine's own flatten mechanisms (fleet EOD sweep at >=15:50 ET, CLAUDE.md's documented 15:50/15:55 hard time-stop, and even the narrower configured time_stop_et=15:40 which a still-open queue item shows does not reliably fire on time) all run AFTER that 3:30pm window opens -- a 10-25 minute gap with zero code, test, backtest, or doctrine coverage anywhere in this repo (confirmed via grep across markdown/, analysis/deep-research/, and the core fleet .py files, all zero hits). Two secondary gaps close/confirm adjacent questions: fleet_broker.py's market-order exit type IS Alpaca-documented as supported for options on both paper and live (no mismatch there), while the live account's options data tier (real OPRA vs the free 15-minute-delayed 'Indicative' feed) remains an explicitly unchecked item in LIVE-FLIP-RUNBOOK §2.4 with no dated progress since it was flagged. The do_not_exercise API exists and is wired but is used nowhere in the actual exit path -- only referenced in test guards asserting it must NOT be called -- meaning there is no DNE fallback if the timing-dependent flatten is late (already observed: one run-eod-flatten-aggressive.ps1 timeout in STATUS.md's self-check log). Overall verdict: this is a genuine, previously-unraised, well-evidenced blind spot that sits squarely on the path to real money and should be closed (tighten/verify the live time-stop to fire meaningfully before 15:25-15:28 ET, and log/reconcile any Alpaca-initiated OPEXC/liquidation activity separately) before any live-flip step, alongside the already-tracked dead-man's-switch and prod-shadow items.

survivors.title: Alpaca's own 3:30pm ET expiration risk sweep can force-close an ITM (or near-OTM) 0DTE long BEFORE the engine's own flatten fires -- unmodeled anywhere
survivors.detail: Alpaca's documented policy: at 3:30pm EST on expiry day it evaluates every position expiring that day; an ITM long the account cannot afford to exercise gets liquidated 'while it's still ITM' at Alpaca's own timing/price, and even 'slightly OTM' positions may also be swept depending on conditions. Every core arm ($5.6K-$6.5K equity) cannot cover exercise of even one SPY contract (100sh x $600+ strike = $60K+ notional), so on a live version of these accounts ANY ITM 0DTE long still open at 15:30 ET falls straight into the liquidate branch. The engine's own exit mechanisms fire LATER than that: the fleet EOD flatten task fires on the >=15:50 ET tick (fleet_eod.py:8-9), CLAUDE.md's documented hard time-stop is 15:50/15:55 ET, and even the narrower internal time_stop_et=15:40 config is documented (queue.md, still status:pending) as NOT firing reliably on time (one real trade's time-stop-eligible exit actually fired at 15:55 via a different mechanism). That leaves a 10-25 minute broker-controlled window, on live money, with a forced exit whose price/slippage/fee behavior has never been backtested, ledgered, or even mentioned in any doc in this repo.

Known cash-subscription floor is $299/mo (Claude Max $200/mo per CLAUDE.md:202, currently paid regardless of paper/live, plus the proposed-but-not-yet-incurred Algo Trader Plus real-time SIP data at ~$99/mo per LIVE-FLIP-RUNBOOK.md:74) -- TradingView Plus is an active recurring cost per memory but its dollar amount appears nowhere in the vault, so $299/mo is a floor, not the true number. Separately, cost-meter.json's claude_code figure is an explicitly-labeled list-price TOKEN ESTIMATE (not a bill, since Max is flat-rate) that ranged $24.58 to $1,908.53/day over the last 7 recorded days (trailing-7d sum $3,308.63) -- I kept this strictly separate from the cash total per the brief's instruction, but it's worth flagging as a compute-intensity signal that dwarfs any arm's edge by 1-2 orders of magnitude, and is already a chronically-unactioned queue item (for a different reason -- alert fatigue, not proportionality). Computing per-arm engine-attributed daily P&L from analysis/trades-enriched.jsonl (independently, cross-checking to the orchestrator's -$7.20/day figure exactly) shows the arm LIVE-FLIP-RUNBOOK names to go live first, safe-2, is NEGATIVE on its full 30-day sample (-$7.20/day) and only turns positive in the small 14-day post-ladder window (+$41.50/day) that the statistical gate has already rejected as unreliable -- while two other active arms (risky-1, safe-3) are already full-sample positive with better risk-adjusted ratios. The 'grow the account to outrun fixed costs' fallback is also structurally blocked: the frozen $1,000 flat max_position_dollars cap already binds tighter than both live-track arms' percentage-of-equity caps at their CURRENT size, so position size (and dollar edge) has already decoupled from equity -- linear scaling from $5.6K is a false assumption, not just an unverified one. Overall verdict: the go-live decision has never been tested against 'is it worth the money,' only against statistics/operations/behavior -- and when tested this session, the answer is marginal at best and negative on the most-trusted sample for the specific arm slated to go first.

survivors.title: The arm slated to go live FIRST (safe-2) has a negative full-sample daily edge -- economically it is the weakest-supported candidate for real money
survivors.detail: LIVE-FLIP-RUNBOOK recommends safe-2 first. But safe-2's full-sample mean daily engine P&L across 30 days is -$7.20 (std $249.45) -- a losing arm on the only sample large enough to have any statistical weight. It only turns positive (+$41.50/day, n=14) in the narrow post-08-11 'tight-ladder' window -- precisely the small-n sample go_live_gate.py's own bootstrap just rejected (CI-lower 0.253-0.329, bar 1.0). Scaling a negative-EV full-sample arm to a bigger account does not fix it: a negative mean stays negative under any linear equity scale-up. Two other active arms (risky-1 +$49.69/day n=26, safe-3 +$32.35/day n=26) are ALREADY full-sample positive with better risk-adjusted ratios (mean/std: risky-1 0.133, safe-3 0.101 vs safe-2's -0.029) -- yet neither is the named first-live candidate.

survivors.title: "Grow the account to cover fixed costs" doesn't work under current frozen params -- the $1,000 flat position cap already decouples edge from equity at today's account sizes
survivors.detail: A natural fix for a marginal per-arm edge is 'let it compound to a bigger account, then the dollar edge scales up.' That assumption is FALSE under the current (frozen-through-09-29) parameter set: max_position_dollars=$1,000 is a flat dollar cap, and it is ALREADY the binding constraint over the pct-of-equity cap for both safe-2 (30% of $5,780 = $1,734 > $1,000) and bold-2 (50% of $5,048 = $2,524 > $1,000) per the params.json doc fields themselves. So position size -- and therefore dollar edge per trade -- has already stopped growing with account equity at the CURRENT ~$5-6K size. Growing equity from $5.6K to $10K or $25K will NOT proportionally grow E unless the flat $1,000 cap is also raised, which directly works against the risk-reduction rationale (PREREG-TIGHT-LADDER-2026-08-28) that just got this cap ratified nine days ago. UNVERIFIED MODEL: under naive linear scaling from ~$5.6K (the assumption the orchestrator asked this reader to test), safe-2's post-ladder edge (E=$41.50/day) would 'break even' against $299/mo fixed cost at equity as low as ~$1,922 (5600 * 14.24/41.50) -- but that number is meaningless both because it's below where min-contract floors bind on the low end, and because the real question (equity needed to rescue the NEGATIVE full-sample edge) has no finite linear-scaling answer at all, since scaling preserves sign.

gaps.angle: J-at-2pm-with-real-money: the human control surface -- what J can actually do from a phone in 60 seconds, and what the engine does to J's own manual trades on a live account
gaps.summary: J's phone-reachable control surface over a live account is thinner than the doctrine implies. The Discord bridge (the only phone channel) is coded and documented as exactly two functions -- an approve/shelve bus for staged Conductor proposals, and free-form Q&A -- with zero execute-side halt/flatten/disarm command; GAMMA_CORE_ARMED is hardcoded in a tracked .ps1 read only at process start, so disarming needs desktop file access plus a scheduled-task cycle. The more serious, previously-unflagged finding: the automated kill-switch mechanism meant to catch an EOD-flatten failure is broken at the filename level in three incompatible ways simultaneously -- the entry gate reads a file with zero writers, eod_flatten.py's own escalation writes a filename nothing reads, and the file that actually exists on disk today (for bold/aggressive, 2 consecutive EOD-flatten failures with an unverified broker position) matches neither convention and is read by nothing. The mechanism that IS actually enforced (circuit-breaker.json's tripped flag) is entirely unaware of any of this and auto-re-arms every morning regardless. On the more reassuring side, two mechanisms the brief worried about turned out to be well-built: manual-trade adoption applies only a protective -50% cap + time-stop (never overrides J's own exit), and a manually-closed position is safely reconciled within ~2 minutes without erroring. Net: the control-surface gap is real and CRITICAL for live money, but it is a broken safety-net wiring bug, not a fundamentally hostile engine design.
